mainTopic: Returning extra land in a sale: רב נחמן's margin rule, רב אשי's questions, and the new משנה on 'measured by the rope'
overview: This amud first finishes רב נחמן's rule about a seller who gave more land than agreed. The buyer may keep a small margin of a רובע (a quarter קב) for each סאה. Extra is returned only if it goes past that margin and is also a meaningful size. רבא challenges him three times from the משנה's measures: nine קבין in a field, half a קב in a garden, and רבי עקיבא's quarter קב. Each time, רב נחמן answers that the משנה means a smaller sale, so the extra really is beyond the margin. רב אשי then asks two sets of questions that stay as תיקו: what if a field became a garden or the reverse, and whether a pit, water channel, public road or row of palms separates the extra land from the seller's own field. Next, a ברייתא teaches that land bordering the seller's field is returned even in a tiny amount. רבין בר רב נחמן reverses the order of a line in the משנה: once the limit is passed, even the allowed quarters go back. Finally, a new משנה begins about a seller who says both 'measured by the rope' and 'whether less or more'. The ruling for the reverse order continues on the next amud. Math to keep in mind: 1 כור = 30 סאה, and 1 סאה = 6 קבין.

steps.title: End of רב נחמן's rule: a large surplus is returned
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן finishes his rule. If, after the allowed margin, there is still extra land that is big enough to matter (nine קבין), it goes back to the seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if there is something extra, that comes to nine קבין, they return it.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of רב נחמן's statement about how much extra land the buyer may keep. It tells us when the extra must be given back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer is allowed to keep a small margin of a רובע per סאה. Only when the extra goes past that margin, and is also a significant size like nine קבין in a field, must it be returned. The next steps test whether the משנה fits this two-part rule.

keyTerms.meaning: nine קבין, an area of field that needs nine קבין of seed

phrases.english: And if there is something extra,
phrases.notes: He means extra land even after the buyer's allowed margin of a quarter קב per סאה.

phrases.english: that amounts to nine kav – they return it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב נחמן's statement, which began earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Extra land that goes beyond the margin and reaches a significant size (nine קבין) is returned to the seller.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule that רבא is about to test three times.

steps.title: רבא challenges from the field case: what if he sold two כור?
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the משנה: extra of nine קבין in a field is returned. He suggests the case is a sale of two כור, where nine קבין would not go beyond the margin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: 'If he left over in the field an area of nine קבין' — isn't that when he sold him two כור?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's rule using the משנה's field case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two כור is 60 סאה, so the margin is 60 quarter-קבין, which is 15 קבין. Nine קבין of extra is less than that margin, yet the משנה seems to say it is returned. That would mean only the size of nine קבין matters, which goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: he challenged him (usually from a משנה or ברייתא)

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Naḥman:
"That if he left over in the field an area of nine kav" –
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה, which says the buyer gives this extra back.

phrases.english: Isn't it where he sold him two kor?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's requirement that the surplus must go beyond the margin of a רובע per סאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a sale of two כור the margin is 15 קבין, so nine קבין is within the margin, yet the משנה says it is returned.

steps.title: Answer: the משנה means a sale of one כור
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the משנה is talking about a sale of one כור, where nine קבין is more than the margin.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is where he sold him one כור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his rule by changing the size of the sale in the משנה's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One כור is 30 סאה, so the margin is only 7½ קבין. Nine קבין is more than that margin, so returning it fits רב נחמן's rule.

phrases.english: No, it is where he sold him one kor.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: a smaller sale size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a sale of two כור, where nine קבין is within the margin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a sale of one כור, where nine קבין goes beyond the 7½-קב margin.

steps.title: רבא challenges from the garden case: what if he sold two סאה?
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the משנה's garden case of half a קב and suggests the sale was two סאה, where half a קב is exactly the margin.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And in a garden, an area of half a קב' — isn't that when he sold him two סאה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries again, this time with the משנה's garden case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two סאה at a רובע each gives a margin of half a קב. So half a קב of extra does not go beyond the margin, yet the משנה says it is returned.

phrases.english: "And in a garden, an area of half a kav" –
Isn't it where he sold him two se'a?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge, following the same pattern as step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's margin requirement, tested on the garden case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a sale of two סאה the margin equals half a קב, so the extra is not beyond the margin, yet it is returned.

steps.title: Answer: the garden sale was one סאה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the garden case is a sale of one סאה, where half a קב is double the margin.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is where he sold him one סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the same kind of answer: the sale in the משנה was smaller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one סאה the margin is just a רובע. Half a קב is twice that, so it clearly goes beyond the margin and must be returned.

phrases.english: No, it is where he sold him one se'a.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: a smaller sale size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The garden sale was two סאה, where half a קב only equals the margin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The garden sale was one סאה, where half a קב is more than the margin.

steps.title: רבא challenges from רבי עקיבא's quarter-קב case
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רבי עקיבא's view in the משנה, that a quarter קב in a garden is returned, and suggests the sale was one סאה, where a quarter קב is exactly the margin.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And according to רבי עקיבא, an area of a רובע' — what, isn't that when he sold him one סאה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a third challenge, using רבי עקיבא's smaller garden measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sale of one סאה the margin is a רובע. Extra of a רובע is not beyond the margin, yet רבי עקיבא says it is returned.

keyTerms.meaning: and according to the words of רבי עקיבא
an area that needs a quarter קב of seed

phrases.english: "And according to the words of Rabbi Akiva, an area of a quarter-kav" –
What, isn't it where he sold him one se'a?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge in the same pattern.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's margin requirement, tested on רבי עקיבא's measure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a sale of one סאה the margin equals a רובע, so the extra is not beyond the margin, yet it is returned.

steps.title: Answer: the sale was half a סאה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that רבי עקיבא's case is a sale of half a סאה, where a רובע is double the margin.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is where he sold him half a סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the third challenge the same way, and his rule stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With half a סאה the margin is only half a רובע. A full רובע of extra is twice that, so it goes beyond the margin. All three cases in the משנה fit רב נחמן's rule once we read them as smaller sales.
steps.whatToRemember: All three of רבא's challenges have the same shape: he picks a sale size where the extra only equals the margin. רב נחמן answers each by halving the sale, so the extra is double the margin. His rule stands: extra land is returned only when it goes beyond the רובע-per-סאה margin and also reaches the משנה's minimum size (nine קבין in a field, half a קב in a garden).

phrases.english: No, it is where he sold him half a se'a.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: a smaller sale size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's case is a sale of one סאה, where a רובע only equals the margin.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא's case is a sale of half a סאה, where a רובע is more than the margin.

steps.title: What if a field became a garden, or a garden became a field?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether the rules for a field or the rules for a garden apply when the land changed type. The question is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: a field that became a garden, or a garden that became a field, what is the law? It stays unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a new question. The משנה gave different amounts for a field and for a garden. What if the land changed from one type to the other?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a field, extra land is given back from nine קבין. For a garden, it is given back from half a קב. If the land was sold as one type and is now the other, we do not know which amount to use. The גמרא finds no answer, so it says תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question he did not know the answer to)
Let it stand: the question stays unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the question is silly or rejected. It means no proof was found either way, so the question stays open.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
A field that was turned into a garden;
phrases.notes: He means a field was sold with extra land, and before the extra was given back, it became a garden.

phrases.english: a garden that was turned into a field: what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבא and רב נחמן back-and-forth and opens a new question built on the משנה's field and garden amounts.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the amount for a field or the amount for a garden applies when the land changed type.

steps.title: If the land is next to the seller's field, even a tiny extra is returned as land
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when the sold field borders the seller's other field, the buyer may give back even a very small amount of extra land itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if the field was next to the seller's field, then even for any small amount, the buyer gives back land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a special case. When the land borders the seller's field, the buyer gives back even a tiny piece of extra land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a small extra piece is not given back as land, because a small separate strip is not useful to the seller. When it touches his own field, he can simply join it to that field. So the minimum amounts from the משנה do not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even tiny

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the background for רב אשי's next set of questions about what counts as being 'next to' the seller's field.

phrases.english: It was taught: If it was next to his field,
phrases.notes: 'His field' means the seller's other field, right beside the extra land.

phrases.english: then even for any small amount,
he gives back land to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with a new case that changes the usual minimum amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the extra land borders the seller's field, any amount, however small, is returned as land.

steps.title: What counts as separating the extra land from the seller's field?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether a pit, a water channel, a public road, or a row of palm trees breaks the 'next to his field' rule. All the questions stay unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: does a pit separate? Does a water channel separate? Does a public road separate? Does a row of palm trees separate? It stays unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי builds on the ברייתא. He asks which kinds of things in between the two fields stop them from counting as next to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's rule works because the seller can easily join the extra land to his own field. If something like a pit or a road sits between them, maybe they no longer count as touching. All four cases are left as תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it count as a separation?

steps.whatToRemember: A small extra piece touching the seller's field is given back as land. Whether a pit, channel, road, or row of palms breaks that connection is never decided.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
A pit: does it count as a separation?
phrases.notes: He means a pit lying between the extra land and the seller's own field.

phrases.english: A water channel: does it count as a separation?
A public road: does it count as a separation?
A row of palm trees: does it count as a separation?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: בּוֹר, מַהוּ שֶׁתַּפְסִיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the ברייתא's 'next to his field' rule reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a pit, water channel, public road, or row of palms stops the extra land from counting as next to the seller's field.

steps.title: The משנה: not just the quarter, but all the extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line: when the extra is more than the allowed amount, the buyer gives back not only the רובע but all the extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he does not give back only the quarter, but all the extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so it can look closely at the wording. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a small extra, up to a רובע for each סאה, may be kept. Once the extra goes past that, the buyer must give back. This line tells us how much he gives back.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a קב, the allowed extra for each סאה
The extra, more than what was agreed

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הָרוֹבַע בִּלְבַד מַחֲזִיר לוֹ,
phrases.english: And he does not give back only the quarter,
but all the extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אֶת הָרוֹבַע בִּלְבַד מַחֲזִיר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רב אשי's questions to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the extra is more than the allowed amount, the buyer gives back all of it.

steps.title: The wording seems backwards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה's 'not only X but even Y' is in the wrong order.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this not the other way around?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא complains that the משנה's wording points the wrong way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not only A, but even B' should end with the bigger new point. The extra beyond the allowed amount is clearly given back. The surprising part is that even the רובע, which the buyer could normally keep, must also be given back. The משנה put the obvious part last.

keyTerms.meaning: Which way is it facing? (the wording is backwards)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the law itself, only about the order of the words in the משנה.

phrases.english: Isn't it the other way around?
phrases.notes: Literally, 'toward which side?' The גמרא is saying the משנה has its two parts in reverse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording quoted in the step before.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of 'not only the quarter, but all the extra' in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bigger new point should come second. Giving back the extra is obvious, and giving back even the allowed רובע is the real news. The משנה has them reversed.

steps.title: רבין בר רב נחמן teaches it in reverse
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב נחמן teaches the משנה the other way: not only the extra is given back, but even all the quarters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב נחמן taught: he gives back not only the extra, but all the quarters too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין בר רב נחמן fixes the problem by teaching the משנה in the correct order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the line ends with the real news. Once the buyer must give back, he cannot keep the allowed רובע per סאה either. He gives back every bit beyond what was agreed.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught (he recited the text this way)
The quarters, the allowed רובע for each סאה

steps.whatToRemember: If the extra is more than a רובע per סאה, the buyer gives back everything beyond what was agreed, including the quarters he could otherwise have kept.

phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Nachman taught:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַמּוֹתָר בִּלְבַד מַחֲזִיר לוֹ,
phrases.english: He gives back not only the extra,
but all of the quarters as well.
phrases.notes: These are the quarter-קב amounts per סאה that the buyer could normally keep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection by flipping the order of the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה with its two parts in the opposite order.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's wording made giving back all the extra sound like the bigger new point.
steps.terutzMaskana: The real new point is that even the allowed quarters are given back once the limit is passed.

steps.title: New משנה: 'Whether less or more' cancels 'measured by the rope'
steps.stepSummary: If the seller says 'measured by the rope, whether less or more,' the words 'whether less or more' cancel the promise of an exact measurement.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a seller says, 'I am selling you land measured by the rope, whether less or more,' then 'whether less or more' cancels 'measured by the rope.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. A seller used two phrases that pull in opposite directions, and the משנה tells us which one counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Measured by the rope' sounds like a promise of an exact size. 'Whether less or more' says small differences don't matter. Here the second phrase wins, so the buyer cannot demand an exact size, and small differences stay as they are.

keyTerms.meaning: Measured by the rope: a promise of an exact measurement
Whether less or more: the size may be a little off
Cancels, makes the other words have no effect

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'whether less or more' lets the seller be off by any amount. It only cancels the promise of exactness. Large differences are still a separate question.

phrases.english: MISHNA: "I am selling you a measured amount, by the rope,
whether less or more" –
the words "whether less or more" cancel
the words "measured by the rope."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ ״מִדָּה בְּחֶבֶל אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ, הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא finished explaining the earlier one about extra land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the seller says 'measured by the rope' and then 'whether less or more,' the words 'whether less or more' cancel the promise of an exact measurement.

steps.title: The reverse order: 'Whether less or more, measured by the rope'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts the opposite case, where the seller says 'whether less or more' first and 'measured by the rope' second. The ruling comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the seller says, 'whether less or more, measured by the rope' –
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its next case, with the same two phrases in the opposite order. It has not given the ruling yet; that comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change from the first case is the order of the phrases. Because the משנה bothers to state this case, the learner should expect that the order of the words may change which phrase wins.

phrases.english: "Whether less or more, measured by the rope" –

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Setup line for the next ruling of the same מימרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Flips the order of the two phrases from step 14 to set up a contrasting case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This step only sets up the case: 'whether less or more' said first, 'measured by the rope' said second. The ruling follows in the next text.
